science.qualification: Uniform photosphere color from the star's LAMOST spectrum. The disc is unresolved: it is darkened toward the limb by the quadratic V-band law Claret & Bloemen (2011) compute from PHOENIX model atmospheres at the star's temperature and gravity, a model rather than a measurement; no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Campaign 1
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 36.6 days, fitted with starry to the K2 mission's own light curve of campaign 1 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 1.2%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.18%, the light's own noise being 0.09%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. Reinhold & Hekker (2020, A&A 635, A43) list the star as a rotator in their table (VizieR J/A+A/635/A43/table2): a rotation period of 36.62 ± 15.65 d in campaign 1, with a periodogram peak of 0.72. The rotation and its period are theirs, taken as published; no criteria were applied to them here. No tilt of this star's axis is known: the map is made at 60°, the middle tilt of axes that point at random. Gaia DR3 lists no other star within 16 arcseconds of it. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: K2 · brightness map made here · Campaign 1

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffc796, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in K2 campaign 1 (June to August 2014): the map's scale, 98% to 102% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 3.5% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: K2 · the star in its color over its brightness map · June to August 2014
